# Task-Technology Fit and Individual Performance

## Localization result

Task-Technology Fit theory links task requirements and technology functionality to fit, utilization, and individual performance.

## Core knowledge

- Task characteristics describe the work demands; technology characteristics describe available functionality and support.
- Fit is the degree to which technology capabilities match task requirements and user needs.
- Fit can affect utilization and performance, while utilization alone may not improve performance when fit is poor.
- The level of analysis and the specific task-technology pairing must be explicit.
- Fit can be measured as perceived fit, profile correspondence, moderation, or other operationalizations, each implying different claims.

## Agent workflow

1. Define the focal task, technology, user, context, and performance criterion.
2. Select a defensible fit conceptualization and measurement strategy.
3. Test alternative explanations such as ability, incentives, experience, and organizational support.

## Limits and stop conditions

- A generic technology-satisfaction measure is not automatically task-technology fit.
- Cross-sectional perceived fit and perceived performance can share method bias.
- Fit can change as tasks, users, and technologies evolve.
